title: A palm-leaf screen and a key at the waist
literal_meaning: A palm-leaf screen at home, a key at the waist.
meaning_odia: ଘରେ ବରଡାର ତାଟି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ ଚାବିକାଠି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଘରର ଚିତ୍ର ସହ ଚାବି ଧରିବାର ଠାଣିକୁ ମିଳାଇ ବାସ୍ତବ ଅବସ୍ଥାଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନକୁ ଟାହି କରାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The verse sets the simple leaf screen against a key carried at the waist. Read editorially, the key becomes a conspicuous sign of having things to secure, while the screen exposes the modest setting. The joke concerns the discrepancy between the display and the circumstances.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A small informal club adopts elaborate signs of office before attending to its basic needs. A reader invokes the saying to question the display. This is an editorial analogy, not a collected use.
cultural_context: The two objects do the work: the frond screen belongs to the dwelling, while the key is carried on the person. Their juxtaposition makes the key stand out as a symbol of possession and control in this editorial reading.
